# daily-research — AI Reference

This is the self-contained AI reference for **daily-research**, an autonomous research feedback engine that runs inside the operator's research repositories and, each morning, explains one external development that matters to the day's repo — what happened, why it matters, and how the repo can use it. It runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p`) on a daily `launchd` schedule. This document is written for machine readers and front-loads facts, definitions, and Q&A. Facts are as of 2026-08-22 (HEAD after ADR-0014).

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents.

## Project Facts

- **Repository**: github.com/shimo4228/daily-research
- **License**: MIT
- **Scheduler**: macOS `launchd` — research at 05:00 (the former 07:00 morning brief was retired by ADR-0009)
- **Runtime**: Bash + Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) + coreutils `timeout`; stdlib-only python3 >= 3.11 (`json` / `tomllib` / `re`) for JSON/TOML parsing in `scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py` — no pip dependencies, no orchestration framework
- **Execution shape (ADR-0010 / ADR-0011)**: each morning `rotation-pick` selects one rotated line (proleptic Gregorian ordinal `date.toordinal()` % number of non-daily lines; cycle order = order in `config.toml`) plus every `daily = true` line. Per picked line: **call 1** = `claude -p` with cwd = the line's repo, model Opus, `--max-turns 55`, 25-minute timeout, one retry on transient failure (a 401 aborts the remaining lines but keeps finished lines' results); **call 2** = fresh-context clarity revision, model Sonnet, `--max-turns 15`, 15-minute timeout, fail-open
- **Lines (tracks)**: 7, mapped 1:1 to research repos — `akc` (agent-knowledge-cycle), `contemplative` (contemplative-agent), `aap` (agent-attribution-practice), `authorship` (authorship-strategy), `ans` (attention-not-self), `desire` (desire-frontier), `edge` (edge-frontier). Six rotate (6-day cycle); `edge` is the daily line (ADR-0013, 2026-08-20) — typically 2 reports per morning
- **Objective function (ADR-0014, 2026-08-22)**: "pick one external development relevant to this repo and explain what happened, why it matters, and how this repo can use it, readable with zero prior context". The subject is the external event, not a verdict on the repo's position; no discovery quota; no proposals or approval requests
- **Theme selection**: 2–3 candidates screened by three yes/no questions — is it new (past-themes dedup), can a primary source be reached in-run, can its use in the repo be named concretely (which ADR / task / open question)? No verdict is stored
- **Input context per run**: the repo's own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded via cwd) + config `context_files` (task ledger, open questions, implementation log) + line brief (`name` / `focus` / `sources` / `context_files` / `self_signals`) + past-themes dedup data + report template
- **Run protocols**: `prompts/repo-research-protocol.md` (call 1) and `prompts/clarity-review-protocol.md` (call 2), both injected via `--append-system-prompt-file`
- **Working state**: `state/<line>/` (watched-sources.md, playbook.md — gitignored) + `past_topics.json` (dedup, gitignored)
- **Repo safety**: mapped repos are read-only, enforced at doctrine, execution, and permission layers — `--allowedTools` scopes Write/Edit to the vault report dir, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`; `--disallowedTools Bash,Task,NotebookEdit` is a deny layer that holds even when the user's default permission mode would widen the allow list
- **Report**: Markdown with YAML frontmatter at `{vault_path}/{output_dir}/{date}_{track}_{slug}.md`; free-form body (~3,000 characters) under three writing rules and a recommended four-part shape; two fixed machine-checked tail sections: 機会メモ and ソース
- **Gates and metrics (ADR-0006, preserved)**: ctl-015 per-line report-existence gate → day class OK / E_PARTIAL / E_NO_REPORT; ctl-016 deterministic lint; `metrics.jsonl` record per day; `DR-Expect:` commit trailers reconciled by `expect-check`; human review via the `/dr-review` skill (weekly). No LLM judge
- **Frozen archive**: `graph.jsonld` — the retired concept-cluster graph (schema.org JSON-LD); no increments after ADR-0008 (schema: `docs/graph-schema.md`)
- **Config format**: TOML (`config.toml` gitignored; `config.example.toml` tracked). `language`, `date_format`, `target_doi`, `[user_profile]` are informational and not read by scripts
- **Tests**: bats — 3 suites (daily-research, e2e-mock, lib) + pytest (`tests/dr_pipeline_test.py`, dev-only `.venv`)
- **Test seams**: `DR_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD` (fix the rotation date), `DR_ONLY_TRACK=<line>` (only that line among today's picks), `DR_FORCE_TRACK=<line>` (one line regardless of rotation). The script also runs from inside a Claude Code session (`lib/env.sh` unsets `CLAUDECODE`)
- **Key files**: `scripts/daily-research.sh`, `scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`, `scripts/check-auth.sh`, `prompts/*.md`, `templates/report-template.md`, `SKILL.md` (Claude Code skill manifest)
- **ADRs**: 0001 research-repo feedback engine (2026-05-27) · 0002 reports as frontier-diff (2026-06-29) · 0003 cross-line knowledge cycle (2026-06-29) · 0004 line restructuring + frontier mode (2026-07-07, superseded) · 0005 line rebalance (2026-07-19, superseded) · 0006 self-improvement loop with human consumer (2026-07-29, preserved) · 0007 return to four 1:1 repo lines (2026-07-31, superseded by 0008) · 0008 per-repo in-context research (2026-08-04, amended by 0009 / 0010 / 0014) · 0009 explanatory reports + brief retirement (2026-08-05, amended by 0014) · 0010 rotation + two-tier in-loop eval (2026-08-13) · 0011 daily line + partial-failure semantics (2026-08-14) · 0012 desire back to rotation (2026-08-18) · 0013 edge daily line (2026-08-20) · 0014 trend-explanation report (2026-08-22, current objective function)
- **Author**: shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya)

## Mapped research repositories

daily-research feeds seven research repositories, one line each (five are DOI-registered). Each `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]` entry names one repo whose directory becomes the run's working directory, so the repo's own operational context defines the area of interest at runtime.

| Line | Research repository | Zenodo DOI | Schedule | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `akc` | agent-knowledge-cycle | 10.5281/zenodo.19200726 | rotation | Agent knowledge cycle, signal-first research, AI knowledge management |
| `contemplative` | contemplative-agent | 10.5281/zenodo.19212118 | rotation | Contemplative AI, meditation science, predictive processing |
| `aap` | agent-attribution-practice | 10.5281/zenodo.19652013 | rotation | AI liability, attribution practice, AI governance |
| `authorship` | authorship-strategy | 10.5281/zenodo.20263316 | rotation | Authorship under AI-mediated diffusion, origin claims, GEO |
| `ans` | attention-not-self | 10.5281/zenodo.20262112 | rotation | Buddhist Abhidharma × computational phenomenology (GWT, predictive coding, IIT, active inference) |
| `desire` | desire-frontier | — | rotation (daily 2026-08-14〜18, ADR-0011 → ADR-0012) | Demand-side frontier: first-person testimony of "nothing left to ask AI", taste / agency / human-bottleneck debates, post-scarcity value |
| `edge` | edge-frontier | — | daily (ADR-0013) | Edge cases of AI use: first-person accounts of out-of-the-ordinary workflows, breakdowns, and whole-life delegation |

## What is daily-research?

daily-research is defined as an autonomous research feedback engine that explains one external development per line per run for the operator's research repositories. Every morning at 05:00, macOS `launchd` runs `scripts/daily-research.sh`, which asks `dr_pipeline.py rotation-pick` for today's lines (one rotated + every daily line) and, for each, runs Claude Code non-interactively (`claude -p`) with the line's repo as the working directory. Each run reads the repo's operational context — CLAUDE.md auto-loads, and the config's `context_files` (task ledger, open questions, implementation log) are read explicitly — then selects a theme, researches it, and writes an explanatory note into an Obsidian vault. A second, fresh-context process revises the note for readability. Orchestration is Bash and prompt files; JSON/TOML parsing is consolidated in a stdlib-only python3 module (`scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`).

## How does a per-repo research run work?

Call 1 is defined as a single Opus run with a seven-step structure: (1) read repo context and state; (2) a diff-first pass over the line's watched sources in `state/<line>/` — `watched-sources.md` holds sources with last-seen state, `playbook.md` holds dated situation→action entries and is delta-updated only; re-surveying is forbidden and the result feeds theme candidates without any obligation to enumerate it in the note; (3) theme selection — 2–3 candidates, three yes/no questions, one theme, no verdict recorded; (4) research with a citation gate — every cited URL must be resolved in-run via WebFetch — plus a self-contamination guard (the operator's own repos never count as external signals); (5) write the note to the vault at `{date}_{track}_{slug}.md`, keeping fact and interpretation apart; (6) update `state/<line>/` (playbook by dated delta only) and `past_topics.json`. Each run is bounded by `--max-turns 55` and a 25-minute external timeout; a transient failure triggers exactly one retry (skipped if attempt 1 already left a report), and a 401 aborts the remaining lines. After the ctl-015 gate, call 2 hands the note to a fresh-context Sonnet process (`--max-turns 15`, 15-minute timeout, Edit limited to that note) that reads as a first-contact reader and fixes comprehension stumbles — defect detection only, no new facts, sources / 機会メモ / frontmatter untouched. Call 2 failure is fail-open: the unrevised (or partially revised) note survives and the day's exit code is unaffected.

## What is the objective function?

The objective function (ADR-0014, 2026-08-22) is defined as "pick one external development relevant to this repo and explain what happened, why it matters, and how this repo can use it — readable with zero prior context". The subject is the external event; the note does not argue for or against the repo's position. The one remaining epistemic rule is to keep fact apart from interpretation: primary-source-verified facts are written as facts, second-hand reports as "reported", and the writer's reading as interpretation. There is no discovery quota. Notes name how the development can be used (which ADR / task / open question) in plain prose but carry no approval requests, no "should", and no step lists — a note is reading material, not a work order. This replaced the ADR-0008 objective ("find immediately executable moves", actionable-tactics notes with a Slack approval brief — retired 2026-08-05 by ADR-0009 because the proposal framing turned every note into a pending to-do) and the ADR-0009 framing ("developments that move the repo's premises", with a corroboration ban, a mandatory refutation section, and a premise-challenge pass — retired 2026-08-22 because the adversarial load made reports unreadable).

## What is the report format?

The format is defined by `templates/report-template.md`: YAML frontmatter (`date`, `category` = track, `tags`, `topic`, `sources` count, `actionable` = number of 機会メモ entries, honestly 0 when none), then a free-form body under three writing rules — lead with the conclusion (3–5 sentences, no approval requests), a background explainer for a first-contact reader (terms defined at first use), and an as-of date on every claim with fact kept apart from interpretation — in a recommended four-part shape: 結論 / 何が起きたか / 背景 / この repo への含意 (~3,000 characters, not linted). Two tail sections are fixed and machine-checked: **機会メモ** (only opportunities with a dated deadline, each as three lines 何を / どこで / 失効日; the single word なし on days with none) and **ソース** (at least five URLs, all resolved in-run). Reports are generated in Japanese by default.

## What are the gates, lint, and metrics?

Three deterministic mechanisms are preserved from ADR-0006. **ctl-015** is the per-line report-existence gate: a line succeeds only if `{date}_{track}_*.md` exists in the vault; the day's final class is OK (all picked lines passed), E_PARTIAL (some failed, ≥ 1 report), or E_NO_REPORT (zero reports) — the last two exit non-zero naming the failed lines (ADR-0011). **ctl-016** is the deterministic report lint: hard fail (notified same day) on a missing `## ソース` section or zero citation URLs; soft findings for a missing `## 機会メモ` (the only entry in `ARTICLE_SECTIONS`), fewer than `min_sources` URLs, or a body under 1,500 characters; each file's `body_chars` is recorded. **metrics.jsonl** appends one record per day: `{date, ts, source, final_class, report_count, fallback_used (= a retry occurred), pass1 (always null since ADR-0008), pass2 (call-1 runs summed: cost / turns / duration_s / tokens_in / tokens_out / searches), clarity_pass ({ran, ok, ...same metrics}, summed across lines, ok only if all succeeded), lint, total_cost}`. `DR-Expect: <metric> <op> <value>` commit trailers (vocabulary: `pass2_turns_p50|p90|max`, `pass2_cost_mean|max`, `total_cost_mean|max`, `fallback_rate`, `report_count_min`, `no_report_count`, `lint_hard_count`; `pass1_*` is permanently INSUFFICIENT_DATA) are reconciled by `expect-check`, and the `/dr-review` skill presents trends weekly. No scores or verdicts from the in-run eval are stored; there is no post-hoc LLM judge.

## How are the mapped repositories kept read-only?

Read-only enforcement is defined at three layers. Doctrine: the research protocol forbids editing the repo and frames every note as reading material, not a deploy. Execution: writes go only to the vault report directory, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`. Permissions: the orchestrator passes `--allowedTools` with `Edit(//abs/path/**)` entries for those three targets (which also authorize Write to the same paths) and `--disallowedTools Bash,Task,NotebookEdit`; the deny list is needed because a user-level `permissions.defaultMode = "auto"` can override an allow list (PoC, 2026-08-22 security review), and deny wins over both. Deploys, ledger updates, and gate decisions belong to the operator's own sessions.

## What happened to the concept-graph pipeline and graph.jsonld?

The concept-graph machinery was retired on 2026-08-04 by ADR-0008. The retired pieces: the central 2-pass pipeline (Opus theme selection over synced repo graphs → Sonnet research), `.repo-graphs/` syncing, the coverage report with coverage/frontier modes, cluster-report with cluster repulsion, theme JSON validation, and daily increments to `graph.jsonld`. The diagnosis: the pipeline could only see repos through concept-graph copies, so theme selection degenerated into graph gap-filling and the output converged on corroboration surveys (a failure mode benchmarked by PseudoBench). `graph.jsonld` is now a **frozen archive** — it keeps the historical Article/Thing cluster data (schema in `docs/graph-schema.md`) but receives no new nodes. Deduplication is handled by `past_topics.json` (with line aliases) and the state layer's watched-sources. The retired code is recoverable from git history.

## Why rotation instead of running every line daily?

On 2026-08-13 a `/dr-review` showed healthy production but a stalled consumption loop: five reports a day exceeded both the operator's reading capacity and the sources' actual rate of change. ADR-0010 replaced daily all-line execution with one rotated line per morning (freeing the budget for Opus on call 1) and added a two-tier in-loop eval: a theme screen before writing and a fresh-context clarity revision after. ADR-0011 (2026-08-14) added `daily = true` lines that run every day outside the rotation and split E_PARTIAL from E_NO_REPORT so partial days do not pollute `no_report_count`; `desire` was daily 2026-08-14〜18 and returned to rotation (ADR-0012); `edge` became the daily line on 2026-08-20 (ADR-0013).

## Why was Mem0 MCP memory removed?

Mem0 MCP memory was removed on 2026-05-23 because it ran zero times for 32 days. It was merged on 2026-02-26, but a missing `.mcp.json` and a hollow health check meant no `mcp__mem0__*` tool was ever called. Its successor, the local `graph.jsonld` concept cluster graph, was itself frozen on 2026-08-04 (ADR-0008). Persistent working state now lives in `state/<line>/` and `past_topics.json` — local files that fail loudly, keeping the pipeline free of external MCP dependencies.

## Why do lines map to research repositories?

Lines map to repositories because fixed topic domains caused structural saturation: under the original generic-trend design, one concept cluster grew to 37% of all topics. ADR-0001 (2026-05-27) remapped tracks to repositories. ADR-0004 added frontier mode and a free-exploration line with cluster repulsion; ADR-0005 rebalanced the lines; ADR-0007 (2026-07-31) abolished free exploration — cluster repulsion had structurally pushed research away from the operator's actual interests — and returned to 1:1 repo lines. ADR-0008 kept that line structure but moved execution inside each repo; later ADRs grew the set to seven lines.

## How is daily-research scheduled and run?

Scheduling is defined by one `launchd` plist: `com.*.daily-research.plist` triggers `scripts/daily-research.sh` at 05:00. The script unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Max plan, not per-token billing) and `CLAUDECODE` (so it also runs from inside a Claude Code session), takes an atomic `mkdir` lock (`.daily-research.lock/` with a `pid` file; a dead-PID lock is stolen), runs a real OAuth probe (a cheap Haiku call — `claude --version` cannot detect expiry), fail-fasts on a legacy config schema, then runs `rotation-pick` and the per-line calls. Every `claude -p` call redirects stdin with `< /dev/null` to prevent MCP stdio conflicts. Logs rotate after 30 days; macOS notifications report success, failure, auth errors, and lint hard fails. After the lines, a vault-side wiki ingest (Pass 3, non-fatal) and the metrics append run. Test seams: `DR_DATE`, `DR_ONLY_TRACK`, `DR_FORCE_TRACK`.

## What models does daily-research use and why?

Call 1 uses Claude Opus: rotation frees the daily budget for one high-quality explainer per line (ADR-0010). Call 2 uses Claude Sonnet: clarity revision is a bounded editing task that benefits from a fresh context more than from peak reasoning. The auth probe is a minimal Claude Haiku call. Runs are invoked with `--append-system-prompt-file` to preserve Claude Code's default capabilities, `--allowedTools` for minimum privilege including path-scoped write access, `--disallowedTools` as a deny layer, `--output-format json` (fed to metrics), and `--no-session-persistence`.

## Is there a quality evaluation framework?

No LLM judge. An LLM-as-Judge framework once scored each report on 6 dimensions; it was suspended in 2026-02 for poor cost-to-value and removed on 2026-06-29. Evaluation is in-loop only (ADR-0010): the theme screen and the clarity revision consume their verdicts inside the same run and store nothing. Structure governs the rest — the citation gate, the deterministic ctl-016 lint, the ctl-015 gate — while the *content* of each note is judged by the human reader and the weekly `/dr-review` (ADR-0006). A post-hoc LLM judge is explicitly not to be revived.

## Who is shimo4228?

shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya) is the author of daily-research and its related research ecosystem — several DOI-registered, idea-rescue research lines including the Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC, 10.5281/zenodo.19200726), the Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice (AAP, 10.5281/zenodo.19652013), authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316), and attention-not-self (10.5281/zenodo.20262112). daily-research maps them as lines. It is a companion engine rather than part of any single research line, and it is the *write* side of a human-mediated knowledge cycle: notes land in a shared vault wiki, and each research line folds findings back into its own repo by hand (ADR-0003).

## Glossary: what do the core terms mean?

- **Line (track)** is defined as a named research stream in `config.toml` that maps 1:1 to a research repository via `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]`; the repo's directory becomes the run's cwd.
- **Rotation-pick** is defined as the deterministic, stateless selection of today's lines: one non-daily line by `date.toordinal() % non-daily line count` (cycle order = config order) plus every `daily = true` line.
- **Daily line** is defined as a line with `daily = true` that runs every morning outside the rotation cycle (`edge` since ADR-0013).
- **Call 1 / Call 2** are defined as the per-line Opus research run and the fresh-context Sonnet clarity revision (defect detection only, fail-open).
- **Explanatory report** is defined as the note format: one external development explained for a zero-context reader, with a deadline-only 機会メモ tail and a ソース section; no proposals.
- **Three-question theme screen** is defined as the in-run selection among 2–3 candidates: new? primary source reachable in-run? use in the repo nameable concretely?
- **Expiry condition (失効条件)** is defined as the valid-until date every 機会メモ entry must carry; knowledge in the LLM space goes stale on a one-week scale, so every claim also carries an as-of date.
- **Diff-first** is defined as the rule that watched sources are checked only for changes since last-seen; re-surveying known themes is forbidden.
- **Watched sources / playbook** are defined as the per-line state files in `state/<line>/`: `watched-sources.md` (sources + last-seen) and `playbook.md` (dated situation→action entries, delta-updated only).
- **Citation gate** is defined as the rule that every cited URL must have been resolved via WebFetch during the run.
- **Self-contamination guard** is defined as the rule that artifacts matching config `self_signals` (the operator's own work) never count as external signals.
- **ctl-015 / ctl-016** are defined as the per-line report-existence gate (→ OK / E_PARTIAL / E_NO_REPORT) and the deterministic report lint (hard: ソース section and citations; soft: 機会メモ, source count, body length).
- **DR-Expect** is defined as a commit trailer `DR-Expect: <metric> <op> <value>` stating the expected effect of a change on `metrics.jsonl`, reconciled by `expect-check` during `/dr-review`.
- **Frozen archive** is defined as the status of `graph.jsonld` after ADR-0008: historical concept-cluster data, no further increments.
